key_insight: Medical multimodal LLMs can be inaccurate in how confident they sound, and this study shows calibration can be improved with a fused interrogation method plus expert LLM assessment.
clinical_relevance: Better confidence calibration may help reduce overtrust in wrong answers and improve reliability in AI-assisted medical visual question answering.
method: Use Multi-Strategy Fusion-Based Interrogation (MS-FBI) to probe model confidence from multiple angles.
Add auxiliary expert LLM assessment to refine confidence estimates.
Compare calibrated confidence against actual correctness on Medical VQA tasks.
evidence_signal: Across three Medical VQA datasets, the proposed approach reduced Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by an average of 40% compared with baseline behavior.
watch_item: The findings come from Medical VQA benchmarks, so real-world clinical deployment may require further validation across specialties, workflows, and patient populations.
paper_title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA
